work_completed: Commit 39e8c5995ee3. (1) `retrieve.py`: the record-graph read now catches only faults that belong to the store: `STORE_MISSING` (no store file), and sqlite errors of exactly the `OperationalError` or `DatabaseError` type (cannot open, no table or column, not a database). The closure facet becomes `{"available": False, "reason": "the record store is missing|unreadable: <why>; no record route or closure"}`, and the closure is not run, even with a ticket or ids. The lexical, semantic and code routes still answer. Without a record graph the authority order is a no-op (`authority.Order(None, …)`); with a graph it is unchanged. Any other fault (a bad query, a `TypeError`) is still raised. (2) `code_route.py`: a code-shaped word takes the route as before. A plain word takes it only when the question has a cue, and the cue words themselves are never looked up as symbols. Final cue list, case-insensitive: call, calls, called, calling, caller, callers, callee, callees, define, defines, defined, definition, definitions, function, functions, method, methods, class, classes, plus backticks or a call form anywhere. One session per code index per process (`_session`), ended at exit through `atexit`. A new session starts when the inode, size or mtime of `home/code.db` changes, or after a question fails. (3) `graph_route.py`: each parsed frontmatter is cached once per process, keyed on the file's size and mtime, and a substring pre-check runs before the title regex. This was the real cost of the check (see discoveries). Builder tests are added to `tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_92_routes.py`.

risks: A reused session keeps answering if the index or tool changes without touching `home/code.db`'s inode, size or mtime (for example the tool binary swapped mid-process). When the whole store file is missing, lexical is gone too (it lives in the same `store.db`), so the code route has no chunks to map its spans onto and returns no evidence. Every `OperationalError` counts as a store fault, as `_graph` already treated it, which includes an SQL syntax error. A project with no store now gets a bundle with the facets unavailable instead of a `STORE_MISSING` refusal, and so the context's `INDEX_UNAVAILABLE` reason no longer appears.
lessons: Profile before trusting the attributed cause: here the daemon starts were a minor cost and the YAML parsing was the main one. `gov accept` reports only counts per KPI line, so a brief that asks for failing names needs another source for them.
